en.title: Different names. Same ingredient.
en.advice: Two medicines can have different brand names but contain the same active ingredient. Check the label before adding another medicine, or ask your pharmacist.

en.title: Check cold medicines, too
en.advice: Some cold and flu products also contain paracetamol. Taking more than one paracetamol-containing medicine can cause an accidental overdose. Ask a pharmacist to check your packets.

en.title: Your prescription, your course
en.advice: Take an antibiotic exactly as prescribed. Do not share it or keep leftovers for another illness. Antibiotics do not treat viral colds or flu.

en.title: More painkillers isn’t always safer
en.advice: Combining anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen and naproxen can increase side effects. Check with a pharmacist before adding another pain medicine.

en.title: Keep your care team in the loop
en.advice: Tell your dentist or doctor about aspirin or clopidogrel before procedures. Do not stop a prescribed antiplatelet medicine on your own.

en.title: Have a plan for sick days
en.advice: Illness can affect blood sugar and hydration. Ask your diabetes care team for a personal sick-day plan rather than changing medicines using this app.

en.title: Take your time getting up
en.advice: Some medicines can cause dizziness. Rise slowly, and avoid driving if you feel dizzy or sleepy. Tell a pharmacist about symptoms that persist.

en.title: Keep the leaflet close
en.advice: Your own medicine packet and leaflet are the first place to check. This reference list is a starting point, not a replacement for advice from a pharmacist.
